chunks: As narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abū al-Maghrāʾ, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
If a Muslim kills a Christian and the family of the Christian wishes to execute him, they may kill him, and they must pay the difference between the two blood monies.

key_terms.أَهْلُ النَّصْرَانِيِّ: the family of the Christian who may seek retaliation
key_terms.الدِّيَتَيْنِ: the two blood monies whose difference must be paid
key_terms.النَّصْرَانِيَّ: the Christian victim referred to in the ruling
key_terms.الْمُسْلِمُ: the Muslim offender in the legal case
key_terms.فَضْلَ مَا بَيْنَ الدِّيَتَيْنِ: the excess amount between the two prescribed blood monies

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a Muslim kills a Christian in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning retaliatory execution when a Muslim kills a Christian. It states that the slain Christian’s family may seek execution, but they must first pay the difference between the two diyyahs.
